[context] Mark 6:13 They cast out many demons, and anointed many with oil who were sick, and healed them.
Mark 6:14 King Herod heard this, for his name had become known, and he said, 'John the Baptizer has risen from the dead, and therefore these powers are at work in him.'
Mark 6:15 But others said, 'He is Elijah.' Others said, 'He is a prophet, or like one of the prophets.'
Mark 6:16 But Herod, when he heard this, said, 'This is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen from the dead.'
Mark 6:17 For Herod himself had sent out and arrested John, and bound him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, for he had married her.
Mark 6:18 For John said to Herod, 'It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife.'
Mark 6:19 Herodias set herself against him, and desired to kill him, but she couldn't,
Mark 6:20 for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. When he heard him, he did many things, and he heard him gladly.
[context] Mark 6:21 Then a convenient day came, that Herod on his birthday made a supper for his nobles, the high officers, and the chief men of Galilee.

[context] Deuteronomy 9:9 when I went up into the mountain to receive the tables of stone, the tables of the covenant, which the Lord made with you, and I was in the mountain forty days and forty nights, I ate no bread and drank no water.
Deuteronomy 9:10 And the Lord gave me the two tables of stone written with the finger of God, and on them there had been written all the words which the Lord spoke to you in the mountain in the day of the assembly.
Deuteronomy 9:11 And it came to pass after forty days and forty nights, the Lord gave me the two tables of stone, the tables of the covenant.
Deuteronomy 9:12 And the Lord said to me, Arise, go down quickly from hence, for thy people whom thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt have transgressed; they have gone aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them, and have made themselves a molten image.
Deuteronomy 9:13 And the Lord spoke to me, saying, I have spoken to thee once and again, saying, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiff-necked people.
Deuteronomy 9:14 And now suffer me utterly to destroy them, and I will blot out their name from under heaven, and will make of thee a nation great and strong, and more numerous than this.
[context] Deuteronomy 9:15 And I turned and went down from the mountain; and the mountain burned with fire to heaven; and the two tables of the testimonies were in my two hands.

[context] Jonah 1:11 And they said to him, What shall we do to thee, that the sea may be calm to us? for the sea rose, and lifted its wave exceedingly.
Jonah 1:12 And Jonas said to them, Take me up, and cast me into the sea, and the sea shall be calm to you: for I know that for my sake this great tempest is upon you.
Jonah 1:13 And the men tried hard to return to the land, and were not able: for the sea rose and grew more and more tempestuous against them.
Jonah 1:14 And they cried to the Lord, and said, Forbid it, Lord: let us not perish for the sake of this man's life, and bring not righteous blood upon us: for thou, Lord, hast done as thou wouldest.
Jonah 1:15 So they took Jonas, and cast him out into the sea: and the sea ceased from its raging.
Jonah 1:16 And the men feared the Lord very greatly, and offered a sacrifice to the Lord, and vowed vows.
Jonah 2:1 Now the Lord had commanded a great whale to swallow up Jonas: and Jonas was in the belly of the whale three days and three nights.
Jonah 2:2 And Jonas prayed to the Lord his God out of the belly of the whale,
[context] Jonah 2:3 and said, I cried in my affliction to the Lord my God, and he hearkened to me, even to my cry out of the belly of hell: thou heardest my voice.

[context] Psalms 54:4 because of the voice of the enemy, and because of the oppression of the sinner: for they brought iniquity against me, and were wrathfully angry with me.
Psalms 54:5 My heart was troubled within me; and the fear of death fell upon me.
Psalms 54:6 Fear and trembling came upon me, and darkness covered me.
Psalms 54:7 And I said, O that I had wings as those of a dove! then would I flee away, and be at rest.
Psalms 54:8 Lo! I have fled afar off, and lodged in the wilderness. Pause.
Psalms 54:9 I waited for him that should deliver me from distress of spirit and tempest.
Psalms 54:10 Destroy, O Lord, and divide their tongues: for I have seen iniquity and gain saying in the city.
Psalms 54:11 Day and night he shall go round about it upon its walls: iniquity and sorrow and unrighteousness are in the midst of it;
Psalms 54:12 and usury and craft have not failed from its streets.
Psalms 54:13 For if an enemy had reproached me, I would have endured it; and if one who hated me had spoken vauntingly against me, I would have hid myself from him.
Psalms 54:14 But thou, O man like minded, my guide, and my acquaintance,
Psalms 54:15 who in companionship with me sweetened our food: we walked in the house of God in concord.
Psalms 54:16 Let death come upon them, and let them go down alive into Hades, for iniquity is in their dwellings, in the midst of them.
Psalms 54:17 I cried to God, and the Lord hearkened to me.
Psalms 54:18 Evening, and morning, and at noon I will declare and make known my wants: and he shall hear my voice.
Psalms 54:19 He shall deliver my soul in peace from them that draw nigh to me: for they were with me in many cases.
Psalms 54:20 God shall hear, and bring them low, even he that has existed from eternity. Pause. For they suffer no reverse, and therefore they have not feared God.
Psalms 54:21 He has reached forth his hand for retribution; they have profaned his covenant.
[context] Psalms 54:22 They were scattered at the anger of his countenance, and his heart drew nigh them. His words were smoother than oil, yet are they darts.

[context] Psalms 118:48 And I lifted up my hands to thy commandments which I loved; and I meditated in thine ordinances.
Psalms 118:49 Remember thy words to thy servant, wherein thou hast made me hope.
Psalms 118:50 This has comforted me in mine affliction: for thine oracle has quickened me.
Psalms 118:51 The proud have transgressed exceedingly; but I swerved not from thy law.
Psalms 118:52 I remembered thy judgments of old, O Lord; and was comforted.
Psalms 118:53 Despair took hold upon me, because of the sinners who forsake thy law.
Psalms 118:54 Thine ordinances were my songs in the place of my sojourning.
Psalms 118:55 I remembered thy name, O Lord, in the night, and kept thy law.
Psalms 118:56 This I had, because I diligently sought thine ordinances.
Psalms 118:57 Thou art my portion, O Lord: I said that I would keep thy law.
Psalms 118:58 I besought thy favour with my whole heart: have mercy upon me according to thy word.
Psalms 118:59 I thought on thy ways, and turned my feet to thy testimonies.
Psalms 118:60 I prepared myself, (and was not terrified,) to keep thy commandments.
Psalms 118:61 The snares of sinners entangled me: but I forgot not thy law.
Psalms 118:62 At midnight I arose, to give thanks to thee for the judgments of thy righteousness.
Psalms 118:63 I am a companion of all them that fear thee, and of them that keep thy commandments.
Psalms 118:64 O Lord, the earth is full of thy mercy: teach me thine ordinances.
Psalms 118:65 Thou hast wrought kindly with thy servant, o Lord, according to thy word.
Psalms 118:66 Teach me kindness, and instruction, and knowledge: for I have believed thy commandments.
Psalms 118:67 Before I was afflicted, I transgressed; therefore have I kept thy word.
Psalms 118:68 Good art thou, O Lord; therefore in thy goodness teach me thine ordinances.
Psalms 118:69 The injustice of the proud has been multiplied against me: but I will search out thy commandments with all my heart.
Psalms 118:70 Their heart has been curdled like milk; but I have meditated on thy law.
Psalms 118:71 It is good for me that thou hast afflicted me; that I might learn thine ordinances.
[context] Psalms 118:72 The law of thy mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver.
